title: Diabetes review
transcript: Good afternoon, Mrs. Lakshmi. Please come in. Your reports came this morning, so let us go through them. Good afternoon, doctor. I was a bit nervous about the sugar levels this time. Your HbA1c is 8.2 percent. Three months ago it was 7.4. So it has gone up, and we need to understand why. Doctor, there were many festivals. Sweets at home every day for two weeks, and I stopped my walks because of the rain. That explains a part of it. Your fasting sugar today is 146 and the after meal reading is 228. Are you taking your tablets regularly? Mostly yes. Metformin I take twice a day. The small one, Glimepiride, I sometimes skip if I am not eating on time. Please do not skip it without telling me, but you are right to be careful. Have you had any episodes of sweating, shaking, or sudden hunger? Twice last month, in the afternoon. I felt shaky and I ate a biscuit and it passed. That is a low sugar episode, and Glimepiride can cause it if you delay meals. So I am going to change the plan a little. Will I have to take insulin? No, not at all. We are not there. We will first adjust the tablets. Continue Metformin 500 milligrams twice a day, after breakfast and after dinner. Okay. Same as now. Yes. Now the Glimepiride 1 milligram, I want you to take only with the breakfast, never on an empty stomach, and only if you are going to eat within half an hour. Okay, I will remember that. And I am adding Januvia 50 milligrams, one tablet once a day in the morning. It lowers the sugar without causing lows, so it is a safer partner for the Metformin. Is it expensive, doctor? My son pays for the medicines now. It costs more than the older tablets, yes. A generic of the same salt, Sitagliptin, is available at a lower price. I will write the salt name so the pharmacist can give you the cheaper one. That will help. Thank you. Your cholesterol was also on the higher side. LDL is 118. Are you still taking the Rosuvastatin? Yes, one at night. Continue Rosuvastatin 10 milligrams at night. For the tingling in your feet that you mentioned last time, I will give Becosules, one capsule daily after lunch for one month. The tingling is worse at night. Is it because of the sugar? It can be. Let me examine your feet. Please take off your sandals. I am checking the pulses and sensation with this small monofilament. Tell me when you feel it. Yes. Yes. I feel it on the left. On the right big toe it is less. Slightly reduced sensation on the right. No wounds or cracks, which is good. Please check your feet every night, and never walk barefoot at home. I always walk barefoot in the puja room. Wear soft chappals even there. Now about food. Reduce white rice to one small bowl, add more dal and vegetables, and no sweets except once a week. My daughter in law will help me plan the meals. Good. Walk for thirty minutes after dinner, even inside the house if it rains. I will also send your urine for microalbumin, to check that the kidneys are not affected. When should I do the blood test again? Repeat the HbA1c after three months. Come to see me after one month with a log of fasting and after meal sugars, two days a week is enough. Okay doctor. So Metformin twice a day, Glimepiride with breakfast, Januvia in the morning, Rosuvastatin at night, and Becosules after lunch. That is exactly right. Well done. If your sugar goes below 70 or you feel shaky, eat something sweet at once and call the clinic. I will. Thank you very much, doctor.
